'''Dhiraj Bora''' (30 September 1951 – 19 June 2021) was an Indian physicist, educationist and professor. Bora, known as a plasma scientist, was a former director of the [[Institute for Plasma Research|Institute of Plasma Research]] located in [[Gandhinagar]], [[Gujarat]].<ref name="ASTU">{{cite web | url=https://astu.ac.in/?page_id=15302| title=PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE OF PROF. DHIRAJ BORA
| publisher=astu.ac.in| date= | accessdate=23 June 2021| author=}}</ref> He was the chief scientist of the [[ITER]] – India. He won the [[Kamal Kumari National Award]] in 2012 in recognition of his contribution to the field of science. In 2016 he was elected as the vice-chancellor of [[Assam Science and Technology University]] and held the post until his death.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.newindianexpress.com/nation/2021/jun/19/renowned-physicist-prof-dhiraj-bora-passes-away-2318697.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210619153619/https://www.newindianexpress.com/nation/2021/jun/19/renowned-physicist-prof-dhiraj-bora-passes-away-2318697.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=19 June 2021|title=Renowned physicist Prof Dhiraj Bora passes away|access-date=26 June 2021|website=[[The New Indian Express]]}}</ref> He died on 19 June 2021.<ref name="sky">{{cite web| url=http://skynewsassam.in/অসমৰ-সুযোগ্য-সন্তান-আন্/| title=পৰ্যায়ৰ প্ৰখ্যাত পদাৰ্থবিজ্ঞানী, শিক্ষাবিদ অধ্যাপক ধীৰাজ বৰাৰ বিয়োগ| publisher=skynewsassam.in| date=19 June 2021| accessdate=23 June 2021| language=as}}{{Dead link|date=January 2024 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

==Early life and education==

Dhiraj Bara was born in Guwahati on 30 September 1951. His father was Lalit Chandra Bora and mother Kusum Bora. He was educated at Senikuthi Primary School in Guwahati.<ref name=yt>{{cite AV media | people=| date= | title=Dhiraj Bora with Diganta Oza| language = Assamese
| url = https://m.youtube.com/watch?v=putCVuSxlDI&feature=youtu.be
| medium=Interview | location=Guwahati | publisher=DOT}}</ref> He was then educated at Manik Chandra Barua ME School. He then joined [[Cotton Collegiate Government H.S. School|Cotton Collegiate School]] but got a scholarship from the Government of India and enrolled in the [[Daly College]] in [[Indore]], [[Madhya Pradesh]] in class VII. After completing class XII in 1968, he enrolled in [[St. Stephen's College, Delhi|St. Stephen's College]], [[Delhi University]] and graduated with a [[Bachelor of Science]] degree. In 1975, he received a Master's degree in [[Experimental physics|Experimental Physics]] from [[Patrice Lumumba Peoples' Friendship University of Russia|People's Friendship University]], [[Moscow]], [[Russia]]. He then received his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD.]] in 1979 from the [[Physical Research Laboratory]], [[Gujarat University]].
